title: Contentment
definition: Contentment is the God-given ability to rest in His wisdom, provision, and presence without being ruled by envy, fear, or craving.
summary: Contentment trusts God in both need and abundance.
christFocus: Jesus is the treasure greater than circumstances, and in Him believers learn to be satisfied in God's care.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Contentment does not mean pretending pain is pleasant or refusing to pray for change. It means learning to trust God's goodness, provision, and presence in every circumstance.

Paul learned contentment in abundance and need. His strength was not in circumstances but in the Lord. Contentment frees the heart from being mastered by comparison, greed, fear, and resentment.

Biblical contentment is rooted in knowing God. The believer can rest because the Father knows what is needed, Christ is sufficient, and grace is present even in weakness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Discontentment can quietly rule the heart through comparison, anxiety, and resentment. Contentment matters because it helps believers find stability in God rather than in changing circumstances.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name the desires that are controlling your peace. Bring them to God in prayer, practice gratitude, pursue faithfulness with what you have, and remember that Christ is enough for today.
